title: Sonny and the Sleepy Rain | Bedtime Story
description: Curl up with Little Sonny the quokka as a soft evening rain comes to the Australian bush. A gentle, calm bedtime story full of cosy sounds and warm sleepy feelings — perfect for winding down before sleep. New episodes of Little Sonny every week.
narration:
The evening was soft and grey when little Sonny the quokka felt the very first drop of rain.

Plip.

It landed right on the tip of his little nose, cool and gentle. Sonny blinked and looked up at the sky.

The clouds had come in slowly, like big sleepy pillows drifting over the bush. And now, one by one, the raindrops began to fall.

Plip. Plip. Plip-plip-plip.

Sonny hurried — but not too fast, because Sonny never hurried too fast — to his cosy spot beneath the big old gum tree. The wide green leaves spread out above him like a roof, and underneath, Sonny stayed warm and dry.

He tucked his paws beneath him and watched the rain come down.

The whole bush began to sing its soft rainy song. Drops pattered on the leaves — pitter, patter, pitter, patter. They trickled down the bark in tiny silver lines. They gathered into little pools that shivered and shone.

Shhhhhh, went the rain. Shhhhhh.

Sonny felt his shoulders go soft and loose. The rain was such a gentle sound. Like the bush was breathing slowly. In, and out. In, and out.

Nearby, a little frog sat happily on a wet green leaf. "Croak," he sang, very pleased. Frogs love the rain.

The possums curled up snug in their hollow. The birds fluffed their feathers and tucked their heads away. And the rain kept falling, soft and steady, all across the sleepy bush.

Sonny watched a single drop slide slowly down a leaf. Down, and down, and down it went, until — plip — it dropped into a little puddle and made a tiny ring.

He watched another. And another. Each one slow and round and quiet.

Sonny's eyes grew heavy.

The rain whispered on. Pitter, patter. Shhhhhh. The air smelled fresh and clean and green, the way the bush always smells when the rain comes to visit.

Warm and dry beneath his big leafy roof, Sonny let out a long, slow, happy sigh.

The clouds above held the whole sky like a soft grey blanket. The rain sang its gentle lullaby. And little Sonny, safe and snug and sleepy, closed his big warm eyes.

Goodnight, little Sonny. Goodnight, soft rain. Goodnight, sleepy green bush.

Sleep now. Everything is calm. Everything is well.
